_note: GH#397 Phase 2, liscor lane. The exception record for this region: every string the lane KEPT against a rule in narrator-bible.md, with the ground it was kept on. Bound to {file, field_path, exact_text} rather than line numbers, matching protected-keeps.json's convention -- a line number re-points silently after a reformat and a field path does not. This file is a RECORD, not an input: no tool reads it, extract_prose.py does not merge it, and it confers no protection by itself. Phase 5's cold read is where these grounds get tested.
_source: review verdict SHIP + fix wave 2026-08-06 (findings M1/M2a/M2b/L2)

petitions.exact_text: Rust holds the bars, not a lock. The draft coming up through them is steady and cold, and it carries the sound of water moving somewhere further in.
petitions.ground: SECTION 7 NEGATION KEEP -- keep-criterion-as-function, ratified verbatim in bible section 7. A barred grate in a city street actively invites the assumption that it is locked, and whether it is locked is information the player acts on: this grate is a real door (entities[12].door_when) into the cisterns, and 'Rust holds the bars, not a lock' is the string that tells the player the descent is available. It corrects a wrong assumption the scene invites and the correction is information the player needs -- not a reframe for effect. NOTE ON THE COUNTER: extract_prose scores neg_correction 2 here, but that is one negation matched by two regexes (',\s*not\b' and 'not a lock.'); semantically the string carries ONE correction. The FOUR stacked shapes the controller named in holdout.json _reserved_named_work were cut by this lane -- 'The draft is steady -- a tunnel, not a pit. The skittering keeps its distance. Something down there has learned to avoid shadows.' -- so the intended reduction happened; this is the one survivor, deliberately.

petitions.exact_text: Thin, immaculate, hungry in a way food will not fix. He holds himself like a duelist and watches hands, not faces.
petitions.ground: SECTION 7 NEGATION KEEP + SECTION 7.3 FILE-CEILING EXCEPTION, CONTROLLER-GRANTED. The negation is MID-SENTENCE ('watches hands, not faces'), which section 7.4 rules is 'far less visible and is not the priority' -- the mechanical shapes the ceiling was written against are 'X is not the same as Y' and 'not P. A Q.', and this is neither. It is voice-load-bearing: 'watches hands, not faces' is the one clause that carries Pisces as a duelist-necromancer who reads threat rather than people, and it is the observe surface a player meets before his graph opens. Cutting it costs characterisation and buys back only a regex hit. THE EXCEPTION BEING RECORDED: with the sewer grate above, street.json carries TWO negation keeps against section 7.3's per-file ceiling of one. Both are ruled keeps, so the file is knowingly one over. It is bounded and paid for -- this lane cut four negation shapes off the grate alone and removed the cellar door's ('Something was dragged in, and not dragged out.') -- so street.json falls from six-plus shapes to two, and the corpus ceiling of eight (section 7.2) is not threatened by two strings in one file. Recorded here rather than left silent because an unrecorded ceiling breach is indistinguishable from a lane that did not read the rule.
petitions.rule: narrator-bible.md section 7.3 (at most one per map file) and section 7.4 (mid-sentence negation deprioritised)

petitions.exact_text: A Gnoll runner, propped against the wall by the stool, legs out, boots still laced. Not asleep. Not far from it.
petitions.ground: GRANTED PETITION (lane-raised, controller-granted). Character-bearing register (bible section 3): a present, visible person, observed. 'Not asleep. Not far from it.' is keep-criterion-as-function -- a Gnoll propped against a wall with his legs out reads as asleep, the scene invites exactly that, and whether he is asleep is information the player acts on (he has a talk_pool and a walk-on line, so he can be spoken to). The correction is also the joke and the joke is at nobody's expense. NOTE ON THE COUNTER: extract_prose scores neg_correction 0 on this string -- 'Not asleep.' has no article, so no regex in RE_NEG_CORRECTION matches it. It is nonetheless a negation SEMANTICALLY, and bible section 10 rules that these bind semantically and not lexically. It is therefore counted as runners_guild.json's ONE section 7.3 negation, and per guard 10.2 the keep CONSUMES the file's allowance rather than sitting outside it. That is why the M2a/M2b re-varying of this file's lamp and mud-table strings deliberately introduced no new negation geometry: the restored 'one corner scrubbed, the ridges start again an inch from it' observation is stated positively for exactly this reason, where the string it restores ('One corner is wiped clean and the rest is not.', closer score 3) was both a negation and a button.
petitions.rule: narrator-bible.md section 7.3 (file allowance, consumed by this keep per guard 10.2)

petitions.exact_text: A dray cart, a missing axle-pin, and a man about one shout from tipping the whole day over.
petitions.ground: GRANTED PETITION (lane-raised, controller-granted), WITH A RECORDED SECTION 3.3 TENSION FOR PHASE 5. Grounds for the keep: one sentence, zero anonymous agents, zero negation, and every element physically present and visible in the scene -- the cart, the absent pin, the man. The wit is compression, not a verdict: the narrator does not tell the reader what the drayman feels or what the scene means, it lists three things and lets the third land. It is also the entry surface for drayman_dispute, whose 'calmed' node is itself a protected keep in protected-keeps.json (the issue's own counterevidence list, 'axle-pin reasoning unfolds messily'). THE TENSION, RECORDED RATHER THAN RESOLVED: bible section 3.3 rules that 'the narrator does not out-perform the character' and is explicitly a read-only principle binding the Phase-5 read and reviewer judgement, not Phase-2 mechanics. This string arguably does out-perform its man -- the drayman's own protected line is deliberately messy and unpolished, and the narrator's introduction of him is neither. The lane's judgement is that the keep is correct and the tension is real, so it is logged here for the Phase 5 cold read to adjudicate with both strings in hand rather than being quietly rewritten now on a principle that was ruled read-only. Counter reading for the record: closer score 1, anon 0, neg 0; 'the whole day over' does NOT trip the section 8 'whole of / the entire' ban (RE_WHOLE requires 'the whole of' or 'the entire').
petitions.rule: narrator-bible.md section 3.3 (narrator does not out-perform the character -- read-only principle, section 11 ruling)
petitions.disposition: GRANTED -- section 3.3 tension noted for Phase 5

petitions.exact_text: A LETTER, sealed in wax gone slightly soft from handling, addressed to no one by name. Inside: impeccable handwriting regrets to inform you of a small disagreement in Invrisil concerning a mutual acquaintance's good name, and would consider it a personal favor — and a professional one — if a stranger to the city might look into it. The witch at Riverfarm keeps the stones, should the distance prove an obstacle. Signed only with a small drawing of a hat. The Guildmistress's clerk says it arrived by very ordinary post, which is itself the strangest part.
petitions.ground: GRANTED PETITION (lane-raised, controller-granted) -- DIEGETIC-DOCUMENT EXCEPTION. A board_rumors 'copy' string is not authorial narration; it is a physical document the player is reading, quoted. Three rules that would otherwise bite are already excepted or satisfied on that basis: (a) section 1.4's two-sentence functional ceiling explicitly excepts 'copy', which is why five sentences is not a breach -- a letter is as long as the letter is; (b) section 8 permits the heading capitals of a 'copy' document, 'whose capitals are the document by definition', and the proxy agrees (caps ['LETTER'], caps_lettering_ctx true); (c) the closing remark sits inside a reported statement attributed to a named in-world speaker -- the Guildmistress's clerk -- so it is a character's aside about the post, not the narrator telling the reader what to think, which is the specific failure the closer ban exists to stop. Flattening it would also cost real content: this letter is the only in-world hook for the Invrisil chain (the hat is Wilovan's signature, and 'the witch at Riverfarm keeps the stones' is the travel affordance), and section 10 guard 1 rules the default action is to leave a string alone.
petitions.rule: narrator-bible.md section 1.4 ('copy' excepted), section 8 ('copy' heading capitals permitted), section 10 guard 1
